o: A pure simulation: the elevator starts at floor 0 and visits requests in order; serving request q from current floor f costs |f - q| seconds. Example 1: 0→2 (2s), 2→1 (1s), 1→4 (3s), 4→3 (1s) totals 7. Example 2 shows repeated requests cost nothing when already there. Constraints are tiny (≤100 floors/requests), so a single linear pass suffices.
k: Travel time between consecutive requests is the absolute floor difference.
Requests are processed strictly in order — no reordering allowed.
n itself is irrelevant beyond validating floor bounds.

a.i: Keep the current floor, accumulate absolute differences to each request in order.
s: For each request, add abs(cur - request) and set cur = request.
a.t: O(len(requests)) — one pass over the request sequence.

w: This is a warm-up; the only traps are forgetting the elevator starts at floor 0 and misreading 'serve in given order'. Likely follow-ups: minimize total time by reordering requests (then it becomes a TSP-like problem), or handle capacity/multiple elevators.
